claim: Overview of KK must-eat dishes: Tuaran noodles with huang jiu/lihing, ngiu chap, sang nyuk mee, sinalau bakas, hinava.
quote: Tuaran Noodles is one of Sabah's most iconic dishes, made with fried egg noodles and often featuring local rice wine (Huang Jiu)... Ngiu Chap (beef noodle)... Sang Nyuk Mee... Hinava is a traditional Kadazandusun dish similar to ceviche.

claim: Tuaran mee is stir-fried springy egg noodles; sinalau bakas is smoked marinated wild boar of the Kadazandusun.
quote: Sinalau Bakas is particularly popular among the Kadazandusun community, made by marinating wild boar meat... smoking them over a fire made from wood and bamboo... Tuaran Mee is a stir-fried noodle dish featuring egg noodles with a distinct, springy texture.

claim: Roundup of 40+ must-try Sabah/KK dishes including tuhau, bosou, pinasakan, nasi linopot.
quote: 43 Must-Try Foods in Kota Kinabalu (2026)

claim: Sang nyuk mee is Sabah's icon pork noodle (distinct from KL); Kim Hing Lee the first coffee shop to serve it (since 1982); a bowl ~RM12.
quote: Kedai Kopi Kim Hing Lee is the first authentic coffee shop serving Sabah Signature Pork Noodle since 1982... A portion of Sang Nyuk Mee costs RM 12, and you can also order additional ingredients, such as pig organs, at an extra cost.

claim: Description of sang nyuk mian as a Sabah soul-warming pork noodle dish.
quote: Sang Nyuk Mian: Sabah's Soul-Warming Noodle Dish

claim: Tuaran Mee Restaurant's signature is Tuaran Mee with lehing (yellow rice wine); seafood version with fish, prawns and vegetables.
quote: their star dish of Tuaran Mee with Lehing, a local yellow rice wine that gives the noodles its superbly unique taste. The seafood Mee Tuaran is highly recommended, served brimming with chunks of fresh fish, succulent prawns, and oodles of vegetables.

claim: In-city Tuaran mee spots: Wan Wan, Fook Yuen, Wun Chiap; best in Tuaran town at Lok Kyun and Yee Fung; price RM8-15, special up to RM25.
quote: popular places include Wan Wan Restaurant, Fook Yuen Kopitiam, and Wun Chiap... the best Tuaran Mee can be found in Tuaran town, especially at Lok Kyun Restaurant and Yee Fung... a plate of Tuaran Mee costs between RM8 and RM15, with seafood or special versions costing more, up to RM25.

claim: Tuaran Mee Restoran in KK city is a dedicated Tuaran mee specialist.
quote: TUARAN MEE RESTORAN, Kota Kinabalu - Restaurant Reviews, Photos & Phone Number

claim: Ngiu chap is beef-cut noodle; KK spots include Kah Hiong (Kolam Centre), Yii Siang laksa ngiu chap (Kolombong), Menggatal Nyuk Pau, with cuts of beef/tripe/tendon/meatballs.
quote: Menggatal Nyuk Pau Baru... beef slices, tripe, tendon, meatballs... Kah Hiong Ngiu Chap, Kolam Centre... Kedai Kopi Yii Siang... Laksa Ngiu Chap specialty.

claim: Best ngiu chap: Loi Hin (Donggongon, 50+ yrs, on 100 Best Coffee Shops), Cheng Wah (Lido, Hainan style since 1961), Kah Hiong, Yii Siang laksa style.
quote: Kedai Kopi Loi Hin... one of the best Ngiu Chap in Sabah for over half a century... Named among Malaysia's 100 Best Coffee Shops... Kedai Cheng Wah... operating since 1961... Yii Siang Hainan Ngiu Chap... creamy laksa variant with coconut milk.

claim: Kim Hing Lee at Sinsuran Complex is one of the oldest sang nyuk mian shops; Jia Siang at Lintas Plaza is a local favourite featured on Taiwan/China/HK TV.
quote: Kedai Kopi Kim Hing Lee... Sinsuran Complex... One of the oldest in town... Kedai Kopi Jia Siang... Lintas Plaza... Appear on few TV shows from Taiwan, China and Hong Kong. Popular with the locals.

claim: Yee Fung at 127 Jalan Gaya has sold Sabah laksa since 1984; the broth has ~20 spices and draws constant queues.
quote: Yee Fung is located at 127 Jalan Gaya... opened its doors in 1984... around twenty ingredients in the soup including red chili, onion, ginger and cinnamon.

claim: Kedai Kopi Yee Fung was named on Asia's 50 Best 'Essence of Asia' list, one of four Malaysian eateries honoured.
quote: Kedai Kopi Yee Fung was featured in 'Essence of Asia' - an unranked listing of Asia's 50 Best Restaurants, making it one of four Malaysian eateries honored.

claim: Hinava is sliced tenggiri (mackerel) cured in lime, bird's-eye chilli, ginger and onion; served at D'Place, The Native Cafe, My Happy Meals, Asiarasa.
quote: Hinava... commonly made from sliced Tenggiri (Mackerel) mixed with bird's eye chilli, ginger, red onion, bitter gourd and lime juice... D'Place Kinabalu... The Native Cafe.

claim: D'Place Kinabalu at Plaza Shell serves Kadazan-Dusun cuisine; ambuyat is sago-starch national dish of Brunei also eaten in Sabah.
quote: D'Place Kinabalu serves traditional Sabahan food... Ambuyat is a starchy, gooey dish made from sago.

claim: The Native Cafe inside Hotel N5 (Penampang) serves the linopot set with tuhau, bambangan, hinava, losun and salted duck egg.
quote: the traditional Linopot set which consists of Tuhau, Bambangan, Hinava, Losun, and Telur Masin (salted duck egg).

claim: Little Sulap (Australia Place, behind The Atkinson) serves authentic Sabahan food, lihing and live/fried butod sago worms; signature Original Sabahan and Ambuyat sets.
quote: Little Sulap Cafe is located to the rear of The Atkinson Place in Australia Place... authentic Sabah specialties, including... lihing (rice wine), butod (sago worm)... signature dishes... are 'Original Sabahan' and 'Ambuyat Set'.

claim: Reviewers single out Little Sulap for extraordinary local Sabahan food: ambuyat and butod.
quote: Extraordinary local Sabahan food: Ambuyat & Butod

claim: Butod (sago grubs) are a high-protein traditional delicacy eaten raw or fried; raw they have a creamy coconut/vanilla taste.
quote: Sabah's traditional sago grub now a popular delicacy... Butod is said to be a high-nutrient food source... can be eaten either raw or fried... taste like coconut milk or vanilla flavour.

claim: Sinalau bakas = smoked wild boar, a traditional Kadazandusun food (sinalau 'smoked', bakas 'wild boar').
quote: Sinalau means smoked and Bakas mean wild boar in Sabah. Sinalau Bakas is a traditional food for the Kadazandusun people of Sabah.

claim: The classic sinalau bakas stalls line AH150 between Tamparuli and Kundasang, roughly halfway from Tuaran to Kinabalu Park, with irregular hours depending on hunting.
quote: the famous stretch of Sinalau Bakas stalls near KK lies along the trunk road to Kundasang from Tamparuli... about half way from Tuaran to Kinabalu Park. The opening day and hour of the stalls are irregular as it depends on hunting.

claim: VOGS Authentic Sinalau Bakas is a sit-down restaurant in Donggongon/Penampang (~10 km from KK) serving smoked wild boar and native cuisine.
quote: VOGS Authentic Sinalau Bakas Restaurant is located in Penampang area, about 10km from Kota Kinabalu, and serves authentic Sinalau Bakas and other native Sabah cuisine.

claim: Welcome Seafood (behind Hilton, Asia City) lets diners pick from the fish tank; three KK branches.
quote: located in the backstreets of Hilton Kota Kinabalu... They have 3 branches throughout the city... choose your favorite ingredients from the fish tank and have them cooked for you.

claim: Welcome Seafood's signature dishes are butter/cream tiger prawn and salted-egg squid; branches in Penampang, Asia City and Inanam.
quote: The cream tiger prawns are worthy of being the signature dish... salted egg squid and white clam soup have garnered rave reviews... branches including Penampang, Asia City, and Suria Inanam.

claim: Live tiger prawns ~RM99 per 300g at Welcome Seafood; steamed preparation preferred over butter for large prawns.
quote: The 300g live prawns (6 pieces) were RM$99, but the butter prawn style was a letdown - the meat became tough so better just eat it steamed.

claim: Suang Tain Seafood in the SEDCO complex (Kampung Air) lets diners select live seafood and veg and specify the cooking.
quote: Suang Tain Seafood Restaurant is located in the SEDCO complex (Kg Air)... customers to select live seafood and fresh vegetables from aquariums and market stalls, specifying how they want their dishes prepared.

claim: Seri Selera Kampung Air (Sedco Square) is an open-air seafood food court with a daily night market; butter prawns, garlic scallops, Sabah veg.
quote: Seri Selera Kampung Air is a seafood food court located in Sedco Square... popular dishes like butter prawns, garlic steamed scallops, and Sabah veggie... hosts a night market daily.

claim: Gayang Seafood on Jalan Sulaman, Tuaran (~25 min from KK) is an open-air estuary hall with live tanks, serves no pork, near Mengkabong water village.
quote: located at Kampung Baharu, Jalan Sulaman, Tuaran... about 25 minutes from Kota Kinabalu City... tanks and buckets of live seafoods including big fishes, clams, crabs, lobster, and mantis prawn. This place serves no pork.

claim: The Filipino Market (opposite Centre Point, waterfront) has hawker stalls of grilled crab, fish, prawn tempura, BBQ squid, stingray and oysters cooked to order.
quote: The Filipino Market is at Jalan Tun Fuad Stephens which lies opposite the Center Point shopping complex... grilled crabs, fish, fried prawn tempuras, barbecued squid, seaweed, and stingrays... pick out your fresh seafood... they will grill or fry it up for you.

claim: KK waterfront night market serves grilled squid, fish and fried rice sets from ~RM50.
quote: For just RM 50, you got grilled squid, a medium-sized fish, and fried rice with chicken on top.

claim: Gaya Street Sunday Market (Sun 06:00-13:00) offers Sabah laksa, kuih cincin, satay, sugarcane juice and pisang goreng; cash, small notes.
quote: open on Sundays from 6:00 AM to 1:00 PM... Laksa Sabah Style... and Kuih Cincin... Satay & Grilled Meats... Pisang Goreng... most vendors preferring cash in small notes.

claim: Fook Yuen at 27 Gaya Street is a traditional kopitiam for kaya toast, soft eggs and roti kahwin (butter+kaya bun) ~RM2.20; egg tarts get mixed reviews.
quote: located at 27, Gaya Street... Kaya toast... The Roti Kahwin being a standout item... famous butter gaya bread one set for RM2.20... One tried the egg tart and the dough was uncooked.

claim: UFO tart (biscuit base, custard, meringue) originated in Sandakan in 1955 from an over-baked batch; sold in KK via Kedai Kopi Mee Ngar branches.
quote: In 1955, a Hainanese cake baker named Fu Ah On... over-baked his tarts... became a traditional cake unique to Sandakan... Kedai Kopi Mee Ngar... branches in Kota Kinabalu (Iramanis, Damai, Telipok, etc.), selling one of the best UFO tarts.

claim: Kuih cincin (palm-sugar/rice-flour ring snack) and amplang are popular edible souvenirs, sold at Gaya Sunday market and the waterfront Handicraft Market.
quote: kuih cincin, or 'ring cakes,'... these palm sugar and rice flour treats... Gaya Street Sunday Market... where I found kuih cincin and Tenom coffee... The Handicraft Market (Pasar Kraftangan)... stalls overflow with dried seafood, amplang.

claim: Kuih cincin is a traditional ring-shaped snack of the Brunei-Malay and Bajau people of Sabah.
quote: Kuih Cincin is a traditional snack of Brunei-Malay and Bajau people in Sabah State of Malaysia.

claim: Tenom is the 'Coffee Capital of Borneo', ~176 km south of Kota Kinabalu.
quote: Tenom is the 'Coffee Capital of Borneo', and it is located approximately 176 kilometres south of Kota Kinabalu.

claim: Yit Foh Tenom Coffee has roasted Robusta since 1960 and runs a café, shop and cottages.
quote: Yit Foh Coffee Factory has, since 1960, operated to produce a perfect blend of the finest roasted Robusta. Yit Foh Tenom opened a cafe and restaurant, a souvenir shop and a few cottages.

claim: Fatt Choi Coffee (Tenom roaster) operates a Kota Kinabalu retail-cafe branch.
quote: Fatt Choi Coffee has a K.K Branch (Kota Kinabalu Branch) that operates as a manufacturer, supply and retail showroom cafe.

claim: Crack Inc. is Sabah's first/leading specialty coffee roaster, established in KK in 2017.
quote: First and leading specialty coffee roaster in Sabah. Established in Kota Kinabalu since 2017, Crack Inc. Coffee Roasters is committed to elevate Specialty Coffee in Sabah.

claim: October Coffee House (Lorong Dewan, Australia Place, 5 min from Gaya St) is the city's only roastery-cafe.
quote: October Coffee House (Gaya), located in Lorong Dewan in Australia Place, is a short 5 minute's walk from Gaya Street... October Coffee House is the only roastery cafe in the city.

claim: A 3-hr Sabah cooking class (hotel pickup, max 10) teaches hinava, tuhau, ambuyat and hill rice for ~US$74.
quote: three-hour cooking class hosted by CTS Travel & Tours includes free pickup... traditional dishes such as Hinava, Tuhau, Ambuyat, and Hill Rice... limited to 10 participants, and costs $74 per person.

claim: Momma's House cooking class includes a local market visit and ends with a family lunch.
quote: followed by a local market visit where you'll see locally-grown produce... Your host family will share their family recipes and you'll sit down with the family to eat lunch.

claim: A combo tour pairs a Borneo traditional cooking class with a visit to a local craft-soda factory.
quote: Borneo Traditional Cooking Class & Local Craft Soda Factory Tour

claim: North Borneo Cruises runs KK's only dinner cruise on the catamaran 'Luna' around the TARP islands and waterfront with an international buffet and live band.
quote: Kota Kinabalu's first and only dinner cruise... 2-hour cruise sails around the TARP Islands and Kota Kinabalu City Waterfront... 28-foot catamaran named 'Luna'... international buffet... with live performances.

claim: Tanjung Aru beach has a casual sunset food court with grilled seafood, satay, chicken wings and coconut.
quote: The beachside food court is famous for affordable local snacks, including grilled seafood, chicken wings, satay, and refreshing coconut water.

claim: After sunset Tanjung Aru turns into a lively food market with vendors selling seafood, fried noodles and desserts.
quote: After sunset, the area transforms into a lively food market, with vendors selling seafood, fried noodles, and traditional desserts.

claim: Kota Belud Tamu is the 'mother of all tamu', run mostly by Bajau ('cowboys of the east') skilled at snacks and handicrafts.
quote: Kota Belud Tamu is the mother of all tamu, with most sellers being Bajau people, the Cowboys of the East, who are very skillful in making yummy snacks and colorful handicrafts.

claim: Tamu are Sabah's weekly open-air markets offering authentic Sabahan food.
quote: Tamu (Weekly Market) in Sabah... The Tamu Market stalls offer authentic Sabahan food.

claim: As of 2 June 2026, 1 MYR ≈ 0.2169 EUR and 1 EUR ≈ 4.61 MYR.
quote: As of June 2, 2026, 1 Malaysian Ringgit equals 0.2169 Euros. This means that 1 EUR is equal to 4.6109 MYR.

claim: Keng Wan Hing on Gaya Street is known for its pineapple custard bun; KK food also includes kon lou mee and Tenom pork roll; waterfront night market for grilled fish.
quote: Keng Wan Hing Coffeeshop... Gaya Street... Pineapple Custard Bun ('bo lo bao')... Kon Lou Mee... 'dry tossed noodles in soy sauce'... Tenom Pork Roll... Waterfront... Fresh grilled fish and seafood street food.

claim: Guide to unique Sabah/KK foods to try while visiting.
quote: Food in Kota Kinabalu- Unique food to try while visiting Sabah
